definitions.definition: Ttor = reals/(2*pi*integers), with normalized measure dx/(2*pi); spatial products and integrals are on this domain.
For an integrable periodic f, Fourier(f)(k)=hat f(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx; the transform extends to distributions by duality.

For every real s, H^s(Ttor) is the completion of trigonometric polynomials with ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z) <k>^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2, <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2). Negative spaces are interpreted as distributions. Homogeneous norms on zero-mean distributions are ||f||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_(k!=0)|k|^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2. Real means hat f(-k)=conjugate(hat f(k)); mean zero means hat f(0)=0.

L2=H^0(Ttor), with ||f||_2^2=(2*pi)^(-1) integral |f|^2 dx. More generally L^p uses the same normalized measure; L^infinity is essential supremum. Sequence ell^2 uses counting measure on Z (or Z\{0} when specified). Time suprema use continuous representatives; derivative norms are essential suprema.

definitions.type: Airy group indexed by real time

definitions.definition: P0(f)=hat f(0), identified with a constant function.
Pnz=I-P0, denoted P in the supplied proof. Fourier projections P_leq(N) and P_gt(N) retain |k|<=N and |k|>N respectively, for N>=0.
Dinv=partial_x^(-1) has Fourier multiplier (i*k)^(-1) at nonzero integer k and zero at k=0. Dinv2=(Dinv)^2 is denoted D^(-2).

For a time interval I=[a,b], Cop_I(f,g,h)=integral_a^b S_(-t) Pnz{Pnz[(S_t f(t))(S_t g(t))]*(S_t Dinv h(t))} dt. Initially this is defined for smooth inputs; the continuous extensions in the source estimates are meant when used for rough inputs.

For an interval I of length at most one, ||f||_X(I)=||f||_(L^infinity(I;L2))+||partial_t f||_(L^infinity(I;H^(-pstar))). Derivatives are distributional time derivatives, with their essential-supremum norms.

definitions.type: family of source periodic Sobolev spaces
definitions.definition: For each real s, Hsrc^s is the space of 2*pi-periodic distributions h with 2*pi*sum_(k in Z)(1+k^2)^s*|Fourier(h)(k)|^2 finite, equipped with the square root of that expression as its norm. The Fourier transform is D002, on the same periodic coordinate Ttor, including the zero mode. Equivalently it is the completion of trigonometric polynomials in this unnormalized norm, with negative orders interpreted distributionally. This is the unnormalized Fourier Sobolev convention used in the Li–Wu source estimates.

L2src=Hsrc^0 on the same torus Ttor. Its norm on functions is (integral_0^(2*pi)|h(x)|^2 dx)^(1/2). Source time L^infinity norms and distributional time derivatives use these spatial norms, continuous representatives for suprema and essential suprema for derivative norms, with the same time coordinate as in D004.

inputs.statement: Let alpha_s in [0,1] and 0<=a_s<=b_s with b_s-a_s<=1. For three functions g_j in L^infinity([a_s,b_s];H^alpha_s) with partial_t g_j in L^infinity([a_s,b_s];H^(-23/14)), define Csrc(g1,g2,g3)=integral_(a_s)^(b_s) exp(t partial_x^3) Pnz{Pnz[(exp(-t partial_x^3)g1)(exp(-t partial_x^3)g2)]*(exp(-t partial_x^3)Dinv g3)}dt. With source unnormalized norms and ||g||_Xsrc=||g||_(L^infinity L2src)+||g'||_(L^infinity Hsrc^(-23/14)), the source gives ||Csrc||_(L2src)<=C*(b_s-a_s)*product_j||g_j||_Xsrc+C*||g_i||_(L^infinity Hsrc^(-23/14))*product_(j!=i)||g_j||_(L^infinity L2src) for each i=1,2,3. If the three inputs are time-independent then ||Csrc||_(L2src)<=C_alpha_s*(b_s-a_s)^alpha_s*product_j||g_j||_(Hsrc^alpha_s). Constants are independent of interval location and Fourier support.

argument.text: From D024 and D003, for every real s and periodic distribution h, the squared Hsrc^s norm is 2*pi times the squared H^s norm. Thus finiteness is equivalent, with the identity map on Fourier coefficients. For the completion descriptions, multiplying the norm by the fixed positive scalar sqrt(2*pi) preserves exactly the Cauchy sequences and the equivalence relation of zero-distance sequences of polynomials. Hence the identity on polynomials extends to inverse identity maps of the completions, agreeing as distributions; it preserves zero mean and reality. Consequently ||h||_(Hsrc^s)=sqrt(2*pi)||h||_(H^s), including s=0 and the L2src/L2 identity by D025 and D004. The same identities hold for time suprema and derivative norms because the time variable and distributional derivative are unchanged. Instantiate E002 on arbitrary I=[a,b] with 0<=a<=b, b-a<=1 and take alpha_s=0 for the time-dependent estimate. Its operator formula is exactly Cop_I because exp(t partial_x^3)=S_(-t). Its derivative exponent is -pstar=-23/14. The source H^s and L2 norms, including derivative and time-supremum norms, equal sqrt(2*pi) times the corresponding normalized norms. Dividing the source inequality by sqrt(2*pi) absorbs the fixed product factor into C and gives the first asserted inequality for every chosen negative-norm slot. Continuous piecewise smooth inputs have distributional derivatives equal to their stepwise derivatives almost everywhere, without point masses, because their values agree at the breaks; hence their finite Xnorm suffices.

produces.statement: For every real s, Hsrc^s and H^s consist of the same periodic distributions, identified by equal Fourier coefficients, and ||h||_(Hsrc^s)=sqrt(2*pi)||h||_(H^s). At s=0 this identifies L2src with L2; the same constant scales time-supremum norms and norms of distributional time derivatives. Reality and zero mean are preserved.

argument.text: For any 0<=sigma<=1 and three arbitrary static mean-zero H^sigma inputs h1,h2,h3, apply E002 with alpha_s=sigma on the same arbitrary interval. The same norm conversion gives ||Cop_I(h1,h2,h3)||_2<=C_sigma |I|^sigma product_j||hj||_(H^sigma). For |I|=0 the integral vanishes. Polynomial approximation and the trilinear bound provide the continuous extension: expand a difference in one slot at a time and use completeness of L2. This proves the static assertion with these arbitrary inputs, which may be renamed f1,f2,f3 in the export.
